This change allows KFP UI to fallback to UI host namespace when no
namespaces are provided when referencing the artifact object store
provider secret, in default kubeflow deployments this namespace is
simply "kubeflow", however the user can customize this behavior by
providing the environment variable "SERVER_NAMESPACE" to the KFP UI
deployment.

Further more, this change addresses a bug that caused URL
parse to fail when parsing endpoints without a protocol, this will
support such endpoint types as <ip>:<port> for object store endpoints,

subject: feat(component): execute in a virtual env (#11326)
message:
feat(component): execute in a virtual env (#11326)

This commit introduces the ability to run the component inside a virtual
environment, which is particularly useful when the Python system site package
directory is read-only, causing pip to fail during the installation of kfp and
other dependencies.

To bypass this issue, a writable temporary directory is selected to create a
virtual environment that inherits the global system site packages. The entire
workflow is then executed from within this virtual environment.

Furthermore, a new field, `use_venv`, has been added to the component
decorator, with a default value of `False`.

subject: feat(sdk/backend): enable parameterization of container images (#11404)
message:
feat(sdk/backend): enable parameterization of container images (#11404)

This change allows component base images to be parameterized using runtime pipeline parameters. The container images can be specified within an @pipeline decorated function, and takes precedence over the @component(base_image=..) argument.

This change also adds logic to resolve these runtime parameters in the argo driver logic. It also includes resolution steps for resolving the accelerator type which functions the same way but was missing the resolution logic. The resolution logic is a generic workaround solution for any run time pod spec input parameters that cannot be resolved because they cannot be added dynamically in the argo pod spec container template.

subject: feat(sdk/backend): Add support for placeholders in resource limits (#11501)
message:
feat(sdk/backend): Add support for placeholders in resource limits (#11501)

The API introduced new fields prefixed with Resource (e.g.
ResourceCpuLimit) to replace the old fields without the prefix. The
Driver hadn't been updated to honor those fields but the SDK started
using them which led to unexpected behavior.

The Driver now honors both fields but prioritizes the new fields. The
SDK now only sets the new fields.

The outcome is that resource limits/requests can now use input
parameters.

Note that pipeline_spec_builder.py was doing some validation on the
limits/requests being set, but that's already handled in the user facing
method (e.g. set_cpu_limit).

Resolves:
https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/issues/11500

subject: fix(backend): Use an Argo Workflow exit lifecycle hook for exit handlers (#11470)
message:
fix(backend): Use an Argo Workflow exit lifecycle hook for exit handlers (#11470)

As described in #10917, exit handlers were implemented as dependent
tasks that always ran within an Argo Workflow. The issue is that this
caused the pipeline to have a succeeded status regardless of if the
tasks within the exit handlers all succeeded.

This commit changes exit handlers to be exit lifecycle hooks on an
Argo Workflow so that the overall pipeline status is not impacted.

Resolves:
https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/issues/11405

subject: feat(backend): Add support for importing models stored in the Modelcar format (sidecar) (#11606)
message:
feat(backend): Add support for importing models stored in the Modelcar format (sidecar) (#11606)

This allows dsl.import to leverage Modelcar container images in an OCI
repository. This works by having an init container prepull the image and
then adding a sidecar container when the launcher container is running.
The Modelcar container adds a symlink to its /models directory in an
emptyDir volume that is accessible by the launcher container. Once the
launcher is done running the user code, it stops the Modelcar
containers.

This approach has the benefit of leveraging image pull secrets
configured on the Kubernetes cluster rather than require separate
credentials for importing the artifact. Additionally, no data is copied
to the emptyDir volume, so the storage cost is just pulling the Modelcar
container image on the Kubernetes worker node.

Note that once Kubernetes supports OCI images as volume mounts for
several releases, consider replacing the init container with that
approach.

This also adds a new environment variable of PIPELINE_RUN_AS_USER to
set the runAsUser on all Pods created by Argo Workflows.

Resolves:
https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/issues/11584

subject: update driver & launcher image handling (#11533)
message:
update driver & launcher image handling (#11533)

This change relies on manifest yamls to specify the launcher & driver
that is pinned to a specific KFP version. The goal is to decouple having
to build launcher/driver at separate stages compared to api server.

This is accomplished by setting the hardcoded default to point to
"latest" and during release, api server is built with this hardcoding,
and the images for driver/launcher are patched into manifests post build
along with the other images.

The apiserver deployment manifest is reformatted using yq so the next
time the release.sh is ran, the user is not surprised by the entire file
reformatting unexpectedly.

added back in commit 6ebf4aae0335424d3bc88175fd06a2b2ba05251f but done in a way

current KFP backend which did not yet support the new fields. In commit
7c931ae20197b2309d7a8462f6ce099882a8f915, the old fields were removed
again but added support for the new field in KFP backend.

This commit addresses the case where a user is using a new SDK but with
a KFP backend prior to 2.4.

chore: fix kfp-kubernetes pipeline spec resolution errors (#11868)

* use packaged pipeline spec in k8s platform pkg

this change updates generate proto code to replace this import to
correctly reference the spec in the kfp.pipeline_spec namespace.

* update to protoc 3.20

generated code attempts to directly create descriptors. This issue is
encountered when trying to use kfp-kubernetes packages with kfp sdk,
forcing the user to downgrade protobuf to 3.20 or lower despite the
kfp sdk and kfp-kubernetes supporting >=4.0. This change resolves
this issue.

updating protoc also requires regeneration of all go and python proto code, as well us updates to the api generate and release images.

subject: fix(sdk): resolve issue when creating pipeline version from pipeline name using the cli. Fixes #11810 (#11866)
message:
fix(sdk): resolve issue when creating pipeline version from pipeline name using the cli. Fixes #11810 (#11866)

It is checked that not both are passed in as parameters, however in the
case of passing in the `pipeline_name` the `pipeline_id` is fetched via
the client and then both values are passed to `upload_pipeline_version`
defeating the initial check and raising an error.

Simply removing the `pipeline_name` argument from the call to
`upload_pipeline_version` fixes this as the `pipeline_id` is always set.

subject: feat(backend/frontend): Add the name field for pipelines and pipeline versions (#11952)
message:
feat(backend/frontend): Add the name field for pipelines and pipeline versions (#11952)

* Add the name field for pipelines and pipeline versions

The API only accepted display_name, which accepted arbitrary characters
but this does not work well in Kubernetes native API mode (Kubernetes
pipeline store) since object names must be a valid DNS subdomain.

This commit adds the name field which is required, but for backwards
compatibility, the API will accept just name or display_name and
duplicate the set value to the unset field. For existing users, they
will only see that there is an extra field of "name" on pipelines and
pipeline versions that is the same value as "display_name".

The database migration logic adds a new DisplayName column and sets the
values to what was in the Name column. Confusingly, the API field
"display_name" used to map the a database column of "Name".

The UI now handles both name and display name but for a simpler user
experience, the display name form fields when uploading a pipeline are
hidden when not in Kubernetes native API mode (Kubernetes pipeline
store) since there is no need to have a display name since there is no
naming restrictions on the name.

Signed-off-by: u4bd2d1599dae6129 <u4bd2d1599dae6129@users.invalid>

subject: fix(backend/sdk): update proto packages (#12067)
message:
fix(backend/sdk): update proto packages (#12067)

Summary of the various changes are below:

--
Update backend protobuf runtime dependencies:

This change comes with a large changeset to accommodate the api breaking
changes introduced with protoc-gen-openapiv2 (grpc-gateway v2+) and other associated (protoc-gen-go, protobuf, etc.).

Some noteworthy changes:

* Newer protoc-gen-go-grpc requires UnimplementedXxxServer struct to help
with forward compatibility and optional method implementations.

Because of this, we can no longer used shared servers for both v1 and v2
APIs. To keep the diff low this change adds a wrapper server to split
them up, whilst keeping shared code co-located.

* use custrom marshaler for grpc-gateway to retain proto field names as json field names

* client go code is updated to accommodate other breaking changes

* presubmit and associated scripts are removed as they are no longer used
by CI.

--
Update testing and CI code to accommodate protobuf upgrades:

This change makes various updates to CI and testing code to achieve
this.

GitHub workflows:

Protobuf dependency installation and management are moved to a separate
action. This allows us to manage versions in one location and remove
redundant code.

Similarly, installation of KFP-Kubernetes, and transitively KFP sdk are
also moved to a separate action.

Presubmit tests now support optional dep installation, allowing us to
instead opt to install dependencies from the CI env instead. This is
to prevent the script from overwriting the python packages we install
via our new re-usable GitHub action.

kfp-k8s and kfp-sdk execution tests have been updated to leverage
kfp-pipeline-spec from the source for runtime tests.

kfp-readiness requirements are moved to their own file, since the
dependency requirement for this script is much smaller than sdk, it makes
more sense to scope this to a smaller, more targeted requirements file.

--
Bump protobuf to 6.x for kfp-kubernetes-platform

The change also includes the re-generated python and go code.

There is also an update to setup.py, where dependencies are split into
separate requirements.txt to supplement dep management via third party
tools.

There are two noteworthy changes to the Makefile:

* Support for installing dependent packages sourced locally, via:
USE_FIND_LINKS, FIND_LINKS_PATH. See inline comments for details.
* Support for fetching dependent protos. Here we re-use the make target
already available from pipeline_spec.

--
Bump protobuf to 6.x for kfp sdk

This change will bump KFP sdk to leverage protobuf 6.x. It also bumps
kfp-pipeline-spec to 0.8.0 which too requires protobuf 6.x.

Note that the version of KFP is also bumped to 2.4.0. This is required
because CI will fail otherwise when it attempts to retrieve KFP 2.3.0
due to a mismatch between kfp sdk 2.13 protobuf requirements (>=4.x,<5),
and kfp sdk 2.14 requirements (>=6.x, <7).

In order to accompany CI, we need to also ensure any CI that tries to
re-compile KFP from source must also install kfp-pipeline-spec from source,
otherwise it will try to download 0.8.0 before it is released. In order to
support this case, there is an env var introduced:

"KFP_PIPELINE_SPEC_PACKAGE_PATH", this var when set will have the executing
pipeline install pipeline-spec from the designated store instead of pypi
(transitively through KFP).

This change is also utilized in some of the kfp.local tests that will
compile and run tests locally via subprocess.

--
Bump protobuf to 6.x for pipeline spec

This change bumps support for kfp-pipeline-spec to 6.x. This is a
significant bump by two major versions. We specifically opt not to support
a range (e.g. >=5.x,<=6.x) because we are bumping protoc to 30.x+ and this
compiler is only compatible with 6.x+.

Accompanying this change is a change to the makefile command. Previously,
the developer was required to hunt down and manually download the protos
originating from the protobuf libraries in git. The makefile will now
download these proto dependencies for the user.

--
Update release and generator dockerfile

fix(backend/sdk): Fix REST API outputs for pipeline versions with invalid platform specs (#12183)

* Skip setting spec.platformSpec when platform spec is empty

An empty platform spec causes a bug where the REST API will not return a
pipeline spec because it errantly thinks the empty platform spec is the

Signed-off-by: u4bd2d1599dae6129 <u4bd2d1599dae6129@users.invalid>

* Fix REST API outputs for pipeline versions with invalid platform specs

When a platform spec did not contain a `kubernetes` platform when
defined as a Kubernetes manifest (e.g. `spec.platformSpec: {}`),
`YamlStringToPipelineSpecStruct` was errantly detecting it as the
pipeline spec when outputting the pipeline version through the REST API.

This caused the REST API to not return a pipeline spec in the case of it
being empty, and caused the UI to load the pipeline and to properly
create a run.

The solution is when translating from the Kubernetes object to a model
representation, the invalid platform specs are not included. This allows
for proper REST API output while also not modifying the user's spec in
the mutating webhook which would cause GitOps tools to always reconcile.

Tasks further in the DAG may expect those side effects. This can lead to
confusing behavior, so the safe approach is use the PVC name in the
cache key. So if the PVC name is the same in the next run, caching can
still work.

subject: feat(sdk): Add notebook components and embedded artifacts support (#12294)
message:
feat(sdk): Add notebook components and embedded artifacts support (#12294)

- Introduce @dsl.notebook_component for notebook-driven components
  - Embeds a .ipynb (or a dir with one .ipynb) into the component
  - Binds dsl.run_notebook(**kwargs) to execute via nbclient at runtime
  - Streams cell outputs; injects parameters (Papermill semantics)
  - Installs default runtime deps when unspecified: nbclient, ipykernel, jupyter_client
- Add embedded artifact support for lightweight components
  - Tar+gzip and base64-embed files/dirs; extract to temp dir at runtime
  - Prepend extracted dir to sys.path; expose __KFP_EMBEDDED_ASSET_DIR/FILE
  - Warn when compressed payload >1MB
- Add EmbeddedInput[...] type (runtime-only)
  - Excluded from component interface; Executor injects an Artifact to embedded asset
- Extend component_factory to support embedded_artifact_path and helper templates
  - Wire into create_component_from_func and command generation
- New DSL helpers and tests
  - Add dsl/notebook_helpers.run_notebook stub and notebook executor template
  - Tests for decorator, parameter injection, streaming, EmbeddedInput, large archive warning
  - Add sample compiled pipeline specs under test_data
- Minor: adjust FutureWarning stacklevel in component creation

Additive SDK feature; no API server changes.

subject: fix: resolve 6 CVEs in frontend server via ESM + k8s client upgrade (#12756)
message:
fix: resolve 6 CVEs in frontend server via ESM + k8s client upgrade (#12756)

* fix: resolve 6 CVEs in frontend server via ESM conversion and dependency upgrades

Resolve CVE-2025-15284 (qs), CVE-2026-24842/CVE-2026-23950/CVE-2026-23745
(tar), CVE-2023-28155 (request), and CVE-2025-13465 (lodash) by upgrading
@kubernetes/client-node from 0.16.3 to 1.4.0 and modernizing the server.

Key changes:
- Migrate test framework from Jest to Vitest 3.x
- Convert server from CommonJS to ESM (type: module, node16 module
  resolution, .js extensions on all relative imports)
- Replace __dirname with import.meta.url equivalent
- Replace node-fetch and portable-fetch with native fetch (Node 22)
- Upgrade @kubernetes/client-node to 1.4.0 (ESM-only, eliminates request,
  tar, and qs from dependency tree, -105 packages)
- Rewrite all k8s API calls from positional args to named parameter objects
- Update return value handling (1.x returns objects directly, no {body}
  wrapper)
- Pin lodash to >=4.17.23 to fix prototype pollution CVE

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* fix: resolve prettier 1.19.1 incompatibility with TS 4.5+ syntax

Prettier 1.19.1 (used in CI) doesn't support `import { type X }` or
`import type { X }` syntax. Convert inline type imports to value imports
and run prettier to fix formatting.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* fix: add @vitest/coverage-v8 dev dependency for CI coverage

CI runs `npm test -- --coverage` which requires @vitest/coverage-v8.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* fix: convert done() callbacks to async/await in all server tests

Replace all done() callback patterns with async/await across 7 test
files. This eliminates vitest 3.x deprecation warnings that caused
non-zero exit codes in CI.

Key changes:
- Convert supertest done callbacks to awaited promises
- Use supertest(app.app) instead of supertest(app.start()) to avoid
  port binding and EADDRINUSE conflicts (see #12757)
- Add afterAll vi.unstubAllGlobals() for files that stub fetch
- Fix fetch mock response bodies to use web ReadableStream where
  handlers call Readable.fromWeb()

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* fix: upgrade vitest to 4.x and fix test compatibility

- Upgrade vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 from ^3.2.4 to ^4.0.18 to
  align with PR #12754 (CRA→Vite migration)
- Migrate vitest.config.ts from deprecated poolOptions.forks.singleFork
  to maxWorkers: 1 (vitest 4 removed poolOptions)
- Fix healthz tests: use toMatchObject instead of supertest .expect(200, body)
  to avoid JSON key ordering sensitivity and buildDate timing race
- Fix GCS constructor mocks: use function keyword instead of arrow functions
  (vitest 4 requires constructable mock implementations)
- Promisify auth server .listen() in beforeEach to prevent EADDRINUSE
  errors from port binding races between test lifecycle hooks

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* test: add server integration tests for K8s client validation

Add dedicated integration tests for validating server-side changes
against a real Kubernetes cluster:

- server-test.js: 21 tests covering static files, API proxy, health
  endpoints, and artifact endpoints
- k8s-integration-test.js: 10 tests validating @kubernetes/client-node
  1.x upgrade (readNamespacedPodLog, createNamespacedPod,
  deleteNamespacedPod, error handling)

These tests are integrated into the e2e-test-frontend workflow and
will run automatically on PRs touching frontend/server/**.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* fix: use default import for crypto-js ESM compatibility

crypto-js is a CommonJS package that exposes SHA1 on its default export.
With ESM `import * as crypto`, SHA1 ends up on crypto.default.SHA1, not
crypto.SHA1, causing "crypto.SHA1 is not a function" at runtime in the
tensorboard handler.

This passed locally because the Kind cluster was running an older image
still using CommonJS require(). CI builds fresh from the PR branch with
ESM compilation, exposing the issue.

feat: add UI smoke test tool for visual regression testing (#12784)

* feat: add UI smoke test tool for visual regression testing

Playwright-based screenshot capture tool for comparing UI across
branches. Supports multiple modes: existing dev server, static build,
and proxy mode (static files + API forwarding to a real backend).
Not wired into CI yet — intended for local use when making UI changes.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* feat: add UI smoke test tool for visual regression testing

Adds a developer tool for catching visual regressions in the KFP
frontend. Captures screenshots of key UI pages via Playwright and
generates side-by-side comparisons with pixel diff percentages.

Primary workflow — compare your branch against master with a live
Kind backend:

  node frontend/scripts/ui-smoke-test/smoke-test-runner.js --compare master

The tool:
- Detects which backend components changed and rebuilds only those
- Manages a Kind cluster lifecycle (start, deploy, port-forward)
- Checks out the base ref via git worktree (fast, offline)
- Builds both frontends and serves them on separate ports
- Captures screenshots of 8 key pages via headless Chrome
- Generates labeled side-by-side comparison images with diff %
- Supports testing someone else's PR via --pr <number>
- Auto-skips backend rebuild when only frontend files changed
- Checks prerequisites at startup and fails fast with install commands
- Guarantees cleanup (worktrees, k8s resources) on all exit paths
- Shows numbered step progress ([3/12] Building 2 backend components)

Also adds a Visual Regression Testing section to frontend/README.md
so developers can discover the tool from where they already work.

subject: fix: switch Python base images to slim to resolve CVEs (#12868)
message:
fix: switch Python base images to slim to resolve CVEs (#12868)

The full python:3.11 image carries a large attack surface with
numerous system-level CVEs inherited from buildpack-deps. Switching
to python:3.11-slim eliminates vulnerable packages not needed at
runtime, including libxml2, libexpat, perl, and nghttp2.

Key CVEs mitigated by removing system packages in the full image:
- CVE-2024-45491 (CRITICAL 9.8) libexpat: integer overflow in dtdCopy
- CVE-2024-45490 (CRITICAL 9.8) libexpat: negative length not rejected
- CVE-2022-49043 (HIGH) libxml2: use-after-free in xmlXIncludeAddNode
- CVE-2024-56171 (HIGH) libxml2: use-after-free in schema validation
- CVE-2025-24928 (HIGH) libxml2: stack buffer overflow in DTD validation
- CVE-2023-52425 (HIGH 7.5) libexpat: DoS via large token reparsing
- CVE-2023-44487 (HIGH 7.5) nghttp2: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset DoS
- CVE-2023-31484 (HIGH 8.1) perl CPAN: no TLS certificate verification

Also pins Google Cloud SDK to v557.0.0 with SHA256 checksum
verification, adds --no-install-recommends, apt list cleanup, and
SDK tarball removal to the visualization server Dockerfile.

subject: feat: add global admin defaults for security context runAsUser/runAsGroup/runAsNonRoot (#12859)
message:
feat: add global admin defaults for security context runAsUser/runAsGroup/runAsNonRoot (#12859)

* feat: add global admin defaults for security context runAsUser/runAsGroup

Expose configmap-driven admin defaults for runAsUser and runAsGroup on
customer workload containers. When configured via pipeline-install-config,
these values are applied at compile time and override SDK-specified values.
Empty by default (feature off) for backward compatibility. Does not affect
executor, driver, sidecar, or init containers.

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

* fix: prevent runtime override of admin security defaults + reject bool UID/GID

Thread admin-configured runAsUser/runAsGroup defaults from compiler to
driver via CLI flags so they are pre-populated in the pod spec patch
before user values are evaluated. This closes the gap where
extendPodSpecPatch always saw a nil SecurityContext (from a fresh patch)
and allowed SDK-specified values to override admin defaults via
strategic merge.

Also reject Python bool arguments for run_as_user/run_as_group since
bool is a subclass of int and True/False silently serialize as UID 1/0.

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

* feat: add runAsNonRoot as admin-configurable security context default

Adds `defaultSecurityContextRunAsNonRoot` to the admin ConfigMap, threading
it through the full API server → compiler → driver chain alongside the
existing runAsUser/runAsGroup defaults. Admin-set values override
SDK-specified values at both compile-time and runtime, matching the
existing enforcement pattern. Also adds `run_as_non_root` parameter to
the Python SDK's `set_security_context()`.

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

- Add missing DefaultRunAsNonRoot threading in CreateJob TemplateOptions

message:
chore(frontend): remove dead deps request, coveralls, swagger-ts-client (#12872)

* chore(frontend): remove dead deps request, coveralls, swagger-ts-client

Remove three unused dependencies that collectively pull in the
deprecated `request` package and its large transitive tree.

## `request` (direct dependency)

Used only by `frontend/scripts/replace_protos.js`, a script that
downloads MLMD proto files from GitHub via `npm run build:replace`.

Evidence the script is dead:
- Only one file in the repo imports `request`: this script (line 19)
- The script was last modified in commit e035a88 (Aug 2021) to bump
  MLMD to v1.2.0
- The most recent MLMD upgrade (commit eaec515, Aug 2023, bumping to
  v1.14.0) updated the proto files directly in git without running
  this script
- `build:replace` is not referenced in any CI workflow, Makefile,
  or other script

frontend. Captures screenshots of key UI pages via Playwright and
generates side-by-side comparisons with pixel diff percentages.

Primary workflow — compare your branch against master with a live
Kind backend:

  node frontend/scripts/ui-smoke-test/smoke-test-runner.js --compare master

The tool:
- Detects which backend components changed and rebuilds only those
- Manages a Kind cluster lifecycle (start, deploy, port-forward)
- Checks out the base ref via git worktree (fast, offline)
- Builds both frontends and serves them on separate ports
- Captures screenshots of 8 key pages via headless Chrome
- Generates labeled side-by-side comparison images with diff %
- Supports testing someone else's PR via --pr <number>
- Auto-skips backend rebuild when only frontend files changed
- Checks prerequisites at startup and fails fast with install commands
- Guarantees cleanup (worktrees, k8s resources) on all exit paths
- Shows numbered step progress ([3/12] Building 2 backend components)

Also adds a Visual Regression Testing section to frontend/README.md
so developers can discover the tool from where they already work.

subject: feat(frontend): upgrade Storybook 6 to 10 with Vite builder (#12940)
message:
feat(frontend): upgrade Storybook 6 to 10 with Vite builder (#12940)

* feat(frontend): upgrade Storybook 6 to 10 with Vite builder

Storybook 6.3.6 uses a webpack5/Babel builder, but the frontend
already runs on Vite 7. Storybook 7 only supports Vite 3–5, so the
minimum compatible version is Storybook 10 (the first release with
vite@^7 support). This upgrade:

- Unblocks the React 18/19 migration by removing Storybook 6's
  transitive deps on @reach/router and create-react-context, which
  are pinned to React 16/17 and gate the peer-dep allowlist.
- Eliminates webpack and Babel from the Storybook build, aligning it
  with the main app's Vite-based toolchain.
- Migrates all 7 story files from CSF 2 to CSF 3 and deletes the
  unsupported Introduction.stories.mdx.

Part of #12891

Changes:
- Replace .storybook/main.js (CJS + webpack) with main.ts (ESM + Vite)
- Replace .storybook/preview.js with typed preview.ts
- Migrate story files to CSF 3 (Meta/StoryObj, fn())
- Remove @babel/core, @babel/preset-*, css-loader, file-loader,
  style-loader, webpack-bundle-analyzer, and all Storybook 6 packages
- Add storybook@10, @storybook/react-vite@10, @storybook/addon-links@10
- Add tsconfig paths for ESM-only Storybook packages
- Clear react-peer-allowlist.json
- Add targeted prettier override for Storybook's peerOptional
  prettier@"^2 || ^3" conflict with our u4fd4f82d417373a6@users.invalid

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

* fix(frontend): add explicit url polyfill lost during Storybook cleanup

The swagger-generated API clients import url.parse/url.format from
the Node.js 'url' module. Previously this resolved to the u536dae714da43baa@users.invalid
browser polyfill installed transitively via Storybook 6's webpack
dependency tree. Removing webpack left the polyfill missing, causing
Vite to externalize 'url' as a Node built-in stub and silently
breaking all API URL construction at runtime.

Add url@^0.11.4 as an explicit production dependency.

subject: fix(frontend): add npm cache retry to prevent EEXIST race condition in Docker build (#12963)
message:
fix(frontend): add npm cache retry to prevent EEXIST race condition in Docker build (#12963)

The frontend Docker build intermittently fails with:
  npm error code EEXIST
  npm error ENOENT: no such file or directory, rename '/root/.npm/_cacache/tmp/...' -> '.../content-v2/sha512/...'

This is a known npm race condition where concurrent download workers try
to write the same package to the cache simultaneously. If one worker
succeeds, the other's rename fails because the tmp source no longer exists
(ENOENT) while the destination already exists (EEXIST).

Add a retry with `npm cache clean --force` on failure to recover from this
transient error. This affects both the build stage (all frontend deps) and
the final stage (server-only deps).

Fixes: https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/actions/runs/22699025197

subject: chore: migrate build system from pip/setup.py to uv workspaces (#12686) (#12770)
message:
chore: migrate build system from pip/setup.py to uv workspaces (#12686) (#12770)

* chore: Migrate build system from pip/setup.py to uv workspaces (#12686)

This commit performs a complete migration of the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK
and related packages from pip-based installation (setup.py, requirements.txt)
to uv workspaces with modern pyproject.toml configuration.

## Motivation

Addresses issue #12686 by adopting uv for faster, more reliable dependency
management and build processes. The uv workspace architecture provides:
- 10-100x faster dependency resolution and installation
- Deterministic builds via uv.lock
- Unified tooling for development, testing, and CI
- Better integration with modern Python packaging standards (PEP 517/518/621)

## Major Changes

### Package Structure
- Created root pyproject.toml with workspace configuration for 4 packages:
  - kfp (sdk/python)
  - kfp-pipeline-spec (api/v2alpha1/python)
  - kfp-kubernetes (kubernetes_platform/python)
  - kfp-server-api (backend/api/v2beta1/python_http_client)

- Created individual pyproject.toml files for each package with:
  - Package metadata and dependencies
  - Build system configuration (hatchling)
  - Optional dependency groups (lint, test, dev, ci, docs)
  - Tool configurations (mypy, pytest, coverage, isort, etc.)

### Removed Files
- All setup.py files (4 packages)
- All requirements.txt, requirements.in, requirements-dev.txt files
- All MANIFEST.in files
- hack/update-all-requirements.sh (no longer needed)
- hack/update-requirements.sh (no longer needed)

### Generated Files
- uv.lock: Lockfile with 196 resolved packages and exact versions
- .github/actions/setup-python/action.yml: Composite action for CI setup
- .github/workflows/check-uv-lock.yml: Workflow to validate lockfile

### CI/CD Updates

**Test Scripts (8 files updated):**
- presubmit-yapf-sdk.sh: Uses `uv run yapf` and `uv run python -m pre_commit_hooks.string_fixer`
- presubmit-isort-sdk.sh: Uses `uv run pycln` and `uv run isort`
- presubmit-docformatter-sdk.sh: Uses `uv run docformatter`
- presubmit-tests-sdk-unit.sh: Uses `uv sync --extra ci` and `uv run pytest`
- presubmit-tests-sdk-client.sh: Uses uv for package installation and pytest
- presubmit-tests-sdk.sh: Uses uv for full SDK tests
- presubmit-test-sdk-upgrade.sh: Uses `uv build --package` instead of `python -m build`
- presubmit-component-yaml.sh: Uses uv sync and uv pip install

**Workflows (6 files updated):**
- kfp-kubernetes-library-test.yml: Replaced custom action with setup-python
- kfp-sdk-tests.yml: Replaced custom action with setup-python
- sdk-docformatter.yml: Uses .github/actions/setup-python
- sdk-isort.yml: Uses .github/actions/setup-python
- sdk-upgrade.yml: Uses .github/actions/setup-python
- sdk-component-yaml.yml: Replaced custom action with setup-python

**Other CI Changes:**
- .github/dependabot.yml: Added pip ecosystem monitoring for uv requirements
- gcpc-modules-tests.yml: Updated to use uv for package installation
- Updated pre-commit config to use uv

### Documentation Updates
- developer_guide.md: Updated installation instructions to use uv
- sdk/python/README.md: Updated development setup instructions
- Various workflow README files updated

### Proto Generation
- Updated Makefiles to work without requirements.in files
- Fixed uv PATH issues in Docker containers by using ~/.local/bin/uv
- Removed README.md requirement from auto-generated packages

### Dependencies
- Added pre-commit-hooks to lint dependencies (required for string_fixer)
- All dependencies now managed through pyproject.toml dependency groups
- Version pins preserved from original requirements files

## Testing

- All 4 packages build successfully with `uv build --package <name>`
- Proto generation works via updated Makefiles
- Local tests pass with `uv run pytest`
- CI test scripts updated to use uv instead of pip

## Breaking Changes

**For developers:**
- Must install uv: `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`
- Replace `pip install -e .` with `uv sync` or `uv pip install -e .`
- Replace `pip install -r requirements.txt` with `uv sync`
- Replace `python -m tool` with `uv run tool`

**For CI/automation:**
- requirements.txt files no longer exist
- Must use uv for package installation
- Use composite action `.github/actions/setup-python` for workflow setup

## Migration Path

Users can continue using pip to install published packages from PyPI.
This change only affects development workflows, not end-user installation.

- This prevents uv from reinstalling/resolving dependencies that are
  already satisfied by the uv.lock file
- Applies to: kfp-sdk-tests, kfp-sdk-unit-tests, kfp-kubernetes-library-test,

without touching the already-installed dependency tree, avoiding version
conflicts and installation errors.

1. uv sync --extra ci (installs all deps from lockfile)
2. Generate proto files
3. uv pip install --no-deps -e packages (install workspace packages only)
4. Run tests in the uv-managed environment

  wheels=(dist/*.whl)

* fix: use default import for crypto-js ESM compatibility

crypto-js is a CommonJS package that exposes SHA1 on its default export.
With ESM `import * as crypto`, SHA1 ends up on crypto.default.SHA1, not
crypto.SHA1, causing "crypto.SHA1 is not a function" at runtime in the
tensorboard handler.

This passed locally because the Kind cluster was running an older image
still using CommonJS require(). CI builds fresh from the PR branch with
ESM compilation, exposing the issue.

test(e2e): migrate frontend integration tests to WDIO v9 and expand coverage (#12915)

* chore(deps): upgrade WebDriverIO suite to v9 and fix minimatch ReDoS

Upgrade all @wdio/* packages and webdriverio from v8 to v9 in the
frontend integration tests. This addresses the minimatch ReDoS
vulnerability (CVE in minimatch <5.1.7, <3.1.3) while keeping the
entire WebDriverIO ecosystem version-aligned.

Changes:
- Bump @wdio/cli, @wdio/junit-reporter, @wdio/local-runner,
  @wdio/mocha-framework, @wdio/spec-reporter, and webdriverio to ^9.24.0
- Remove @wdio/selenium-standalone-service (no v9 release; only used
  in local DEBUG mode, not CI)
- Rename deprecated `host` config to `hostname` for wdio v9
- Remove deprecated wdio config options: `sync`, `coloredLogs`,
  `deprecationWarnings`

Supersedes #12914 which only bumped @wdio/local-runner to v9 while
leaving all other @wdio packages on v8, creating a version mismatch.

Switch to slim base images for components and frontend (#12927)

* Switch to slim base images for components and frontend

Use slim variants of base images in component definitions and frontend
Dockerfile to reduce container image sizes. This targets components
that do not require system tools like git or gcc at runtime.

Changes:
- frontend: node:22.19 -> node:22.19-slim
- Google Cloud starry_net components: python:3.9 -> python:3.9-slim
- Google Cloud forecasting: python:3.8 -> python:3.8-slim
- Snowflake components: python:3.11 -> python:3.11-slim
- PyTorch launcher sample: python:3.11 -> python:3.11-slim

The SDK default base image (python:3.11) is intentionally not changed
as lightweight Python components rely on system tools (e.g. git) that
are not available in slim images.

subject: fix: prevent stale ci-passed labels (#13095)
message:
fix: prevent stale ci-passed labels (#13095)

* fix: prevent stale ci-passed labels

- remove stale ci-passed labels immediately on synchronize and reopened
- re-add ci-passed only after a successful CI Check on a label-eligible PR
- guard against race condition where an older workflow_run could re-add
  the label after a new push by comparing head SHAs
- check whether ci-passed label exists before removal to avoid silently
  swallowing real API errors
- add issues: write permission required by the Labels API
- remove artifact handoff from ci-checks.yml; derive PR metadata directly
  from workflow_run

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

* fix: handle ci-passed label eligibility transitions

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

* fix: guard label triggers to avoid wasted CI runner minutes

Promote label eligibility checks from step-level to job-level conditions
so ineligible PRs are 'skipped' instead of 'success', preventing wasted
downstream workflow_run triggers. Guard 'unlabeled' events to only react
to eligibility-relevant label changes (needs-ok-to-test removal in
ci-checks, ok-to-test removal in add-ci-passed-label), avoiding the
50-min polling loop restart on unrelated label changes like size/L or
lgtm.

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

* fix: add symmetric guard for labeled events in CI check workflow

Skip the polling loop when unrelated labels (size/L, lgtm, etc.) are
added to an eligible PR. Only the 'ok-to-test' label addition can
change eligibility, mirroring the existing 'unlabeled' guard.

Signed-off-by: u07cdfddff917d5ea <u07cdfddff917d5ea@users.invalid>

* test(compiler): update golden files for KFP_RETRY_INDEX env var

Add KFP_RETRY_INDEX={{retries}} to all compiled workflow golden files,
reflecting the new commonEnvs entry added in argocompiler/common.go.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: u07cdfddff917d5ea <u07cdfddff917d5ea@users.invalid>

* fix(compiler): inject KFP_RETRY_INDEX only on retry executor templates

{{retries}} resolves to empty string in Argo for templates without a
retryStrategy. Adding it to commonEnvs caused every non-retry component
to trigger an unnecessary pod-annotation Kubernetes API call in the
launcher fallback path, which was adding latency and causing flaky E2E
test failures.

Restrict KFP_RETRY_INDEX injection to the executor template specifically
when a retryStrategy is present. Non-retry components continue to use
the pod-annotation fallback path (reads workflows.argoproj.io/node-name
and parses the (N) suffix), while retry components get the cheaper
env-var fast path.

Update the 134 affected compiler golden files accordingly.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: u07cdfddff917d5ea <u07cdfddff917d5ea@users.invalid>

* fix(compiler): revert spurious security context additions in golden files

The previous golden file regeneration (-updateCompiledFiles=true) picked up
pre-existing security context that the compiler already generates but was
never reflected in golden files. The workflow_matcher skip-if-nil logic means
these were always tested as 'don't check this field', so including them in
golden files is unnecessary noise.

Revert all golden files to master state except pipeline_with_retry.yaml,
which now correctly includes KFP_RETRY_INDEX only in the executor template
that has a retryStrategy.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

subject: fix(backend): resolve use_secret_as_env pipeline params in ParallelFor (#13128)
message:
fix(backend): resolve use_secret_as_env pipeline params in ParallelFor (#13128)

* fix(sdk): propagate platform-config inputs across sub-DAG boundaries

When `use_secret_as_env()` (or other Kubernetes platform helpers) reference
a `PipelineParameterChannel`, the channel was not registered in the task's
`_channel_inputs`. This meant the compiler did not "punch through" the
parameter across sub-DAG boundaries (e.g. ParallelFor), causing the driver
to fail with "parent DAG does not have input parameter".

Additionally, the platform config references were not rewritten to use the
prefixed parameter names that the compiler creates when surfacing parameters
through sub-DAG boundaries.

Changes:
- Add `ensure_channel_input()` shared helper in common.py that registers
  PipelineChannel values in `task._channel_inputs` for sub-DAG propagation
- Call it from `parse_k8s_parameter_input()` (secrets) and
  `_assign_pvc_name_to_msg()` (PVC mounts) for consistent behavior
- Add `_rewrite_platform_config_input_references()` that rewrites both
  `componentInputParameter` and `taskOutputParameter` references in
  platform config when tasks are inside sub-DAGs
- Pass parent component inputs and DAG task list to
  `platform_config_to_platform_spec()` for rewriting context
- Apply rewriting in both `build_spec_by_group()` and exit handler paths

Fixes #13078

subject: fix(security): prevent SQL injection in pageToken parameter via field name validation (#13127)
message:
fix(security): prevent SQL injection in pageToken parameter via field name validation (#13127)

* fix(security): prevent SQL injection in pageToken parameter via field name validation

The pageToken parameter in list APIs (e.g. /pipeline/apis/v1beta1/pipelines)
is a Base64-encoded JSON containing database field names (KeyFieldName,
SortByFieldName, ModelName, etc.) that were concatenated into SQL queries
without validation, allowing SQL injection attacks.

Add validateIdentifierName() with regex ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,127}$ and
call it for all identifier fields in token.unmarshal() before any SQL query
is constructed.

Attack vector: pageToken with crafted KeyFieldName (e.g. EXTRACTVALUE(...))
Security issue: HASI2026112-23
Severity: High

Signed-off-by: u2fe749dedd9da67e <u2fe749dedd9da67e@users.invalid>

* fix(security): validate filter keys in pageToken to prevent SQL injection

The Filter embedded in pageToken was deserialized without key validation,
allowing forged tokens with malicious keys like "Name) OR 1=1 --" to reach
SQL construction. Added Filter.ValidateKeys() to filter package and called
it during token.unmarshal(), reusing the existing validateIdentifierName
helper. Qualified keys like "table.Column" are supported by validating each
segment separately. Added regression tests for malicious filter token inputs.

Signed-off-by: u2fe749dedd9da67e <u2fe749dedd9da67e@users.invalid>

* fix: correct error message from 'Invalid package token' to 'Invalid page token'

Corrects misleading error message in list.go and list_request_util.go
to help API consumers correlate the error with the pageToken parameter.

Signed-off-by: u2fe749dedd9da67e <u2fe749dedd9da67e@users.invalid>

* fix(security): close first-page SQL injection via metric sort (CVE-2023-6570)

The previous pageToken validation only protected subsequent-page requests.
First-page ListRuns requests with sortBy=metric:<name> still concatenated
the user-supplied metric name directly into SQL structure (column alias and
JOIN predicate), allowing SQL injection without a pageToken.

Fix (jeffspahr's architectural suggestion):
- Split SortByFieldName (user-facing, pagination state) from SortBySQLColumn
  (safe SQL identifier) in list.token
- Extend Listable.GetField to return (fieldName, sqlColumn, ok); regular
  fields return fieldName==sqlColumn; metric fields return the fixed alias
  "sort_metric_value" as sqlColumn so user input never reaches SQL structure
- Parameterize the run_metrics JOIN predicate (name=?) instead of string concat
- Use fixed alias "sort_metric_value" in SELECT and column propagation instead
  of opts.SortByFieldName
- Validate SortBySQLColumn in pageToken unmarshal (must pass identifier check)
- Add regression test TestListRuns_MetricSortInjectionSafe

Files changed: list/list.go, list/list_test.go, model/{run,experiment,job,
pipeline,pipeline_version,task}.go, storage/run_store.go,
storage/run_store_test.go, server/list_request_util_test.go

Signed-off-by: u2fe749dedd9da67e <u2fe749dedd9da67e@users.invalid>

* fix(list): allow hyphens in metric sort names for pagination

Metric names (e.g. "log-loss", "val-accuracy") legitimately contain
hyphens, but token.unmarshal() was validating SortByFieldName with the
SQL identifier regex (^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$) which rejects "-".
This caused page-2 requests with hyphenated metric names to fail with
"Invalid sort field name".

Fix: introduce validateMetricName() with a relaxed pattern that allows
hyphens, and use it in unmarshal() when SortBySQLColumn equals the
fixed metric alias (model.MetricSortSQLAlias). The metric name is
only ever used as a bind parameter value — never as a SQL identifier —
so allowing "-" is safe.

Add TestListRuns_HyphenatedMetricSort to confirm both pages of a
metric:log-loss sort succeed without error.

unhandled promise rejection because the method is called outside the

Wrap the body in a try/catch that logs the error, preventing the
unhandled rejection while keeping the rest of the page functional.

message:
fix(frontend): add root ErrorBoundary and loading indicators (#13245)

* fix(frontend): add root ErrorBoundary and loading indicators

- Wrap <Router /> with <ErrorBoundary> in index.tsx so unhandled
  render-time errors show a styled Banner instead of a white screen.
- Upgrade ErrorBoundary fallback from raw HTML to Banner component
  for visual consistency with the rest of the UI.
- Add CircularProgress loading indicator to RecurringRunDetailsV2FC
  while the recurring run query is in flight.
- Add CircularProgress loading indicator to InputOutputTab while
  artifact data is being fetched.

  tests for RecurringRunDetailsV2FC and InputOutputTab.

Signed-off-by: u95279418408cc456 <u95279418408cc456@users.invalid>
Made-with: Cursor

* fix(frontend): key ErrorBoundary by location to allow navigation recovery

Address review: the root ErrorBoundary latched error state permanently,
making the entire SPA unrecoverable after any page throw. Wrap it in a
LocationKeyedErrorBoundary that keys by location.key, so React remounts
the boundary (clearing latched state) on every navigation.

Signed-off-by: u95279418408cc456 <u95279418408cc456@users.invalid>
Made-with: Cursor

* fix(frontend): fix V2FC loading spinner test matching Router's spinner

The Router now also renders CircularProgress in its loading state
(merged via #13246), so the test's getByRole('progressbar') matched
the Router's spinner immediately—before the Router's query fired—
leaving mockOnce entries unconsumed and leaking into subsequent tests.

Wait for the Router to finish loading before asserting V2FC's spinner.

Signed-off-by: u95279418408cc456 <u95279418408cc456@users.invalid>
Made-with: Cursor

* fix(frontend): reset getRecurringRunSpy mockOnce queue between tests

vi.clearAllMocks() does not clear the mockOnce queue. When the
loading-spinner test exits before V2FC's queryFn fires, the queued
mockReturnValueOnce(new Promise(() => {})) leaks into subsequent tests.

Add getRecurringRunSpy.mockReset() in beforeEach to explicitly clear
the once queue before re-setting the default implementation.

subject: feat(manifests): add init containers for startup ordering to all critical deployments (#12970)
message:
feat(manifests): add init containers for startup ordering to all critical deployments (#12970)

* feat(manifests): add init containers for startup ordering to all critical deployments

Add init containers to critical deployments to wait for their
dependencies before starting, preventing CrashLoopBackOff during fresh
installations.

Deployments and their dependencies:
- metadata-grpc: waits for MySQL/Postgres via pipeline-install-config
- metadata-writer: waits for metadata-grpc-service:8080
- ml-pipeline (apiserver): waits for database + metadata-grpc-service
- ml-pipeline-persistenceagent: waits for ml-pipeline:8888
- ml-pipeline-scheduledworkflow: waits for ml-pipeline:8888

All init containers use a unified template with WAIT_HOST/WAIT_PORT env
vars and an identical retry script (12 retries x 5s = 60s timeout).
Alpine 3.23 tag is hardcoded in deployment YAMLs rather than via
kustomize images sections to avoid release.sh wildcard corruption.
Overlay patches for db/postgres use $patch: replace to override the
init container env vars with the correct host and port.

Add OpenShift-specific JSON patches (remove-sc-init.json) to strip
init container securityContext so the restricted SCC can assign UIDs
from the namespace range.

Fixes #12702

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

* fix(manifests): increase init container timeout from 60s to 300s

CI logs show MySQL takes ~67s to start, and the full dependency chain
(MySQL → metadata-grpc → ml-pipeline) takes ~100s. The 60s timeout
caused persistenceagent and scheduledworkflow init containers to timeout
and restart, defeating the purpose of startup ordering.

Increase MAX_RETRIES from 12 to 60 (300s total) to accommodate slow
CI runners and cold-start image pulls.

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

* fix(manifests): resolve init container WAIT_HOST in metadata overlays

The init container for metadata-grpc-deployment used $(MLMD_DB_HOST) as
its WAIT_HOST env value, but MLMD_DB_HOST is a kustomize replacement
placeholder that only gets resolved by the replacements rule in each
overlay's kustomization.yaml -- and that rule targets the main
container's args, not the init container's env.

Rendering with kubectl kustomize confirmed the literal $(MLMD_DB_HOST)
passed through to the final manifest. At runtime, Kubernetes left it
unresolved, so nc tried to connect to host "$(MLMD_DB_HOST)" and the
init container failed after the timeout.

Fix by hardcoding the Service name in each overlay's patch:
- db overlay: metadata-db
- postgres overlay: metadata-postgres-db

Also add both overlays to manifests/kustomize/hack/test.sh so future
renderings get smoke-tested in CI.

Reported-by: u7ad2b67d7fff52e3

Signed-off-by: u0a0b5ccf281cdc88 <u0a0b5ccf281cdc88@users.invalid>

* fix(manifests): validate WAIT_HOST and WAIT_PORT in init containers

Add an early guard to every wait-for-* init container script so that
when WAIT_HOST or WAIT_PORT is empty/unset, the container fails fast
with a clear error instead of silently retrying nc against an empty
target for the full MAX_RETRIES window.

subject: fix(frontend): download v2 directory artifacts as tar.gz. Fixes #7809 (#13320)
message:
fix(frontend): download v2 directory artifacts as tar.gz. Fixes #7809 (#13320)

* fix(frontend): download v2 directory artifacts as tar.gz

KFP v2 output artifacts may be directories (S3 prefixes) rather than
single objects. The artifact download handler currently 500s with
NoSuchKey when the user clicks download on a directory artifact.
Fall back to listing the prefix and streaming the contents back as a
.tar.gz.

Pages listObjectsV2Query at 300 keys per request to stay under
fast-xml-parser's 1000 entity-expansion cap; each Contents entry
contributes ~2 ETag entities, so 1000-key pages fail past ~500
objects in a directory.

Fixes #7809

Signed-off-by: uf871c52538228b19 <uf871c52538228b19@users.invalid>

* fix(frontend): address review on directory artifact download

- Sanitize tar entry names: strip leading slashes and "." / ".."
  segments to prevent tar-slip path traversal on extraction.
- Guard the internal listObjectsV2Query call with a runtime check so a
  future minio upgrade that removes the method fails fast with a clear
  error instead of throwing deep inside a stream pipeline.
- Convert listObjectsUnderPrefix to an async generator so the tarball
  starts streaming as soon as the first object is listed, instead of
  buffering every key in memory before the response begins.
- Build Content-Disposition via an RFC 5987 helper so user-controlled
  keys with spaces, quotes, or non-ASCII characters can't break the
  header or produce confusing fallback filenames.
- Add unit tests for isNoSuchKeyError and listObjectsUnderPrefix, and
  integration tests covering the directory tar.gz fallback (happy path,
  empty prefix 404, tar-slip protection, safe Content-Disposition).

Signed-off-by: uf871c52538228b19 <uf871c52538228b19@users.invalid>

* fix(frontend): match real u278803f8b7ddea80@users.invalid listObjectsV2Query Promise shape

u278803f8b7ddea80@users.invalid made listObjectsV2Query async and returns
Promise<ListObjectV2Res>; previously it returned an EventEmitter
transformer. The directory-artifact fallback was wrapping the call in
a `new Promise((resolve, reject) => stream.on('error'/'data', ...))`
adapter, which crashes at runtime against 8.0.7 with
`stream.on is not a function` before any keys are listed.

Type the internal accessor as Promise-returning and await the call
directly. Update both unit and integration test mocks so they mirror
the real client's runtime shape (resolve a page record) instead of
masking the bug behind an EventEmitter mock.

Signed-off-by: uf871c52538228b19 <uf871c52538228b19@users.invalid>

* fix(frontend): bound directory artifact previews with a text summary

The run details panel calls Apis.readFile with a small peek size to
render an inline preview. Previously the directory-artifact fallback
ignored peek and would list every object under the prefix and stream
the entire gzip archive — opening run details on a large output could
fetch megabytes just to render a few KB.

When peek > 0 and the key is a directory, answer with one capped
listObjectsV2Query call (no pagination) and return a small text
summary like:

  Directory artifact "model" — 5 file(s). Download to view contents.

For directories larger than the cap, the summary reads "50+ file(s)"
based on the isTruncated flag. Empty prefixes still 404. Downloads
(peek === 0) keep the full .tar.gz behavior.

Adds summarizeDirectoryUnderPrefix in minio-helper, with unit tests
covering complete listings, truncated listings, empty prefixes, and
the maxKeys cap. Adds integration tests asserting the preview path
makes exactly one list call, performs no per-child getObject fetches,
and surfaces the truncated count correctly.

Signed-off-by: uf871c52538228b19 <uf871c52538228b19@users.invalid>

subject: fix(backend): recursive DAG execution state propagation (#13322)
message:
fix(backend): recursive DAG execution state propagation (#13322)

When a container task completes, the launcher updates only its immediate
parent DAG's status via UpdateDAGExecutionsState. Sub-DAGs (ParallelFor,
If/Else/Elif, nested pipelines) never propagate their completed/failed
state upward. This causes ExitHandler groups to get stuck as "Running"
after all tasks finish, and nested pipeline DAGs to never reach
COMPLETE/FAILED.

This change refactors UpdateDAGExecutionsState to:

1. Use runtime iteration_count for ParallelFor DAGs instead of
   compile-time total_dag_tasks, which gives incorrect expected child
   counts when iteration count differs from the compiled value.

2. Recursively propagate state upward through the DAG chain. After
   marking a DAG as COMPLETE or FAILED, the function reads parent_dag_id
   from the DAG's custom properties, fetches the parent DAG, and
   recursively checks/updates its state. Propagation stops at the root
   DAG (parent_dag_id == 0), whose lifecycle is managed by Argo/the API
   server.

3. Properly handle errors from PutDAGExecutionState, which were
   previously silently ignored.

Fixes #13321
Fixes #11979

workflow spec, so executionSpec.ServiceAccount() is never empty for
V2 pipelines. This caused the user-specified service account from

Remove the guard so setDefaultServiceAccount is called unconditionally,
matching the existing behavior in RunWorkflow.

Fixes #13311

subject: feat(frontend,backend): show actual retry start time for pipeline runs. Fixes #12845 (#13009)
message:
feat(frontend,backend): show actual retry start time for pipeline runs. Fixes #12845 (#13009)

* feat(frontend,backend): show actual retry start time for pipeline runs

When a pipeline run is retried, the Start time shown in the UI previously
reflected the original scheduled time rather than the actual retry execution
time. This was misleading when debugging failures or SLA compliance issues.

Changes:
- backend: refactored RetryRun in resource_manager.go to update the full
  run object before persisting, preserving all existing fields correctly
- frontend: added getActualStartTime() in RunDetailsV2.tsx that reads the
  last RUNNING entry from state_history to determine the actual start time
- frontend: updated getDetailsFields() to show "Started at" as the actual
  execution time and conditionally insert "Scheduled at" when the two times
  differ

Fixes #12845

Signed-off-by: uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5 <uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5@users.invalid>

* fix(frontend): fall back to scheduled_at when RUNNING state update_time is undefined

getActualStartTime() returned undefined when a RUNNING state_history entry
existed but its update_time was not set, causing "Started at" to display "-"
even though a scheduled time was available.

Added a guard so that a missing update_time is treated the same as having no
RUNNING entries, and the fallback to scheduled_at is applied correctly.

Signed-off-by: uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5 <uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5@users.invalid>

* style(frontend): fix prettier formatting in RunDetailsV2.tsx

Signed-off-by: uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5 <uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5@users.invalid>

* test(frontend,backend): add tests for retry start time logic
- frontend: add tests for getActualStartTime() covering last RUNNING
  update_time, undefined update_time fallback, and equal-timestamp case
- frontend: fix timestamp comparison to use getTime() instead of
  formatDateString() to avoid locale/formatting false-equals
- frontend: insert 'Scheduled at' relative to 'Started at' using
  findIndex instead of a hard-coded index
- backend: add TestRetryRun_PreservesRunFields to verify UUID, name,
  experiment ID, FinishedAtInSec reset, and State after retry

Signed-off-by: uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5 <uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5@users.invalid>

* fixed formatting error

Signed-off-by: uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5 <uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5@users.invalid>

* fix(frontend): scan all RUNNING entries for most recent defined update_time

Previously getActualStartTime only checked the last RUNNING entry's
update_time, falling back to scheduled_at even if earlier RUNNING entries
had a valid time. This could hide the actual retry start time in
partially-populated state_history.

Now scans backwards through state_history to find the most recent RUNNING
entry with a defined update_time, only falling back to scheduled_at if
none are found.

Signed-off-by: uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5 <uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5@users.invalid>

* fix(backend): remove redundant embedded field selector in test

golangci-lint QF1008: RunDetails is embedded in Run, so access
FinishedAtInSec and State directly without the RunDetails prefix.

Signed-off-by: uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5 <uf881f5c6a6a8dfd5@users.invalid>

* fix(tests): address review feedback on retry tests

- frontend: add missing await before userEvent.click() in 3 new
  retry start time test cases to fix flaky CI failures
- backend: extend TestRetryRun_PreservesRunFields to assert

* fix: resolve artifact lookup and graph assertion for retry nodes (#13500)

When templateDefaults.retryStrategy is applied globally, Argo wraps each
template execution in a retry parent node. This causes two CI failures:

  https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5025

  https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5027

subject: fix(backend): inject user identity header in scheduled-workflow-controller for multi-user auth (#13472)
message:
fix(backend): inject user identity header in scheduled-workflow-controller for multi-user auth (#13472)

* fix(scheduled-workflow): inject user identity header for multi-user auth

In multi-user mode, the scheduled-workflow-controller calls CreateRun via
gRPC to the API server. Previously, only an Authorization: Bearer <token>
header was attached (when a service-account token file was present). The
API server's HTTPHeaderAuthenticator also requires a user identity header
(e.g. kubeflow-userid), and rejects the request with 'Unauthenticated:
Request header error: there is no user identity header' when the token
volume is not mounted.

This commit adds two new CLI flags to the controller:
  --userIdentityHeader: the header name (e.g. kubeflow-userid)
  --userIdentityValue:  the value to set (e.g. the controller SA identity)

When both are set, the controller injects the header into the gRPC
outgoing metadata alongside the existing Bearer token. Both flags default
to empty strings, making the feature fully opt-in -- existing single-user
deployments are unaffected.

The multi-user kustomize deployment patch is updated to pass these flags
using the controller's own service account identity, derived from the
pod namespace via the downward API.

Signed-off-by: u08cd8f170f164394 <u08cd8f170f164394@users.invalid>

* fix(scheduled-workflow): validate user identity gRPC metadata key

Address review feedback on the user identity injection:
- Normalize the configured userIdentityHeader to lowercase and validate it
  against gRPC metadata key rules in NewController, failing fast at startup
  instead of risking failed requests during reconciliation.
- Clarify the --userIdentityHeader/--userIdentityValue flag help to state
  that the value is injected as outgoing gRPC metadata (not an HTTP header).
- Add unit tests for the key normalization/validation helper and for
  NewController rejecting a malformed key.

Signed-off-by: u08cd8f170f164394 <u08cd8f170f164394@users.invalid>

* fix(scheduled-workflow): pass user identity via env vars, not pod args

The multi-user deployment patch set the user identity flags via the pod
spec 'args' field. The controller image has no ENTRYPOINT and invokes the
binary through its CMD (a shell that maps env vars to flags), so setting
'args' replaced the entire CMD and the container tried to exec
'--userIdentityHeader=...' as the binary, crash-looping with:

  exec: "--userIdentityHeader=kubeflow-userid": executable file not found in $PATH

Follow the existing convention instead: expose the configuration as the
USER_IDENTITY_HEADER / USER_IDENTITY_VALUE env vars and map them to the
--userIdentityHeader / --userIdentityValue flags in the Dockerfile CMD.
The multi-user patch now sets those env vars (defaulting to empty, so
single-user deployments remain unaffected).

Signed-off-by: u08cd8f170f164394 <u08cd8f170f164394@users.invalid>

* fix(manifests): source multi-user auth params from shared ConfigMap

Hardcoding USER_IDENTITY_HEADER, KUBEFLOW_USERID_HEADER, and
KUBEFLOW_USERID_PREFIX directly in each deployment patch meant
customized installs (different header name or renamed service account)
would silently diverge after upgrade.

- Add pipeline-multi-user-params ConfigMap with KUBEFLOW_USERID_HEADER
  and KUBEFLOW_USERID_PREFIX as the single source of truth
- Source those values via configMapKeyRef in the api-service,
  pipelines-ui, and scheduled-workflow deployment patches so all three
  components always agree on the header name
- Replace the hardcoded service account name in USER_IDENTITY_VALUE
  with spec.serviceAccountName via the downward API so renamed
  service accounts are handled automatically

Signed-off-by: u08cd8f170f164394 <u08cd8f170f164394@users.invalid>

* misc: use proper words as variable names and spelling fixes

Signed-off-by: u08cd8f170f164394 <u08cd8f170f164394@users.invalid>

* fix(scheduled-workflow): reject grpc- reserved prefix in metadata key validation

Keys beginning with "grpc-" are reserved by the gRPC runtime and silently
dropped at the transport layer, defeating the fail-fast guarantee of
normalizeAndValidateMetadataKey. Add an explicit check and a corresponding
test case.

Signed-off-by: u08cd8f170f164394 <u08cd8f170f164394@users.invalid>

* fix: use USERID_HEADER as variable name to stay consistent with central dashboard

Signed-off-by: u08cd8f170f164394 <u08cd8f170f164394@users.invalid>

* fix(manifests): centralize multi-user userid params in pipeline-install-config

Move USERID_HEADER and USERID_PREFIX out of the dedicated
pipeline-multi-user-parameters ConfigMap and into the global
pipeline-install-config, so the multi-user identity contract has a single
source of truth shared by the API server, UI, and scheduled-workflow
controller.

Make the KUBEFLOW_USERID_HEADER/KUBEFLOW_USERID_PREFIX and
USER_IDENTITY_HEADER env var references optional so customized installs
that omit these keys fall back to component defaults instead of failing
to start.

subject: fix(ci): prevent ci-passed label when workflows await approval (#13629)
message:
fix(ci): prevent ci-passed label when workflows await approval (#13629)

* fix(ci): prevent ci-passed label when workflows await approval

Three bugs caused ci-passed to be added while pull_request workflows
were still stuck in action_required state:

1. The approve workflow did not trigger on reopened events, leaving
   workflows unapproved after close/reopen cycles.
2. A race condition caused the approve workflow to query for pending
   runs before they were created, finding zero runs to approve.
3. The CI Check polling (allcheckspassed) only sees GitHub Check Runs,
   but workflows awaiting approval do not create check runs, making
   them invisible to the poll.

Fix: add reopened trigger to the approve workflow, add a retry loop
to wait for runs to appear before approving, and add an approval gate
step in CI Check that blocks polling until all action_required runs
clear. Also bump allcheckspassed to v2.4.0.

* fix(backend): do not retry permanent plugin failures at terminal report

Every OnRunEnd failure previously requested a terminal-report retry,
so a permanently broken MLflow configuration (config unavailable,
missing settings, unresolvable credentials) left completed runs in
retry forever: the run never received the persistedFinalState label
and its workflow could never be garbage collected.

Classify plugin terminal-sync failures as transient or permanent at
the source: syncMLflowRuns only requests a retry when the MLflow API
calls themselves failed, while config-class failures are recorded in
plugins_output as PLUGIN_FAILED and reported as nothing-to-retry. The
dispatcher still retries when the plugin output could not be
persisted. RunPluginHandler.OnRunEnd now returns the retry signal
alongside the error.

Covered by dispatcher-level tests for both classifications.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* fix(backend): finalize run when workflow is deleted before terminal report

The reported-version preflight returned NotFound when the workflow CR
was already gone, which the persistence agent treats as permanent, so
the run row was never updated to its terminal state.

Proceed with the reported terminal state when the preflight Get
returns NotFound: the run row is finalized and plugin terminal sync
runs first, and the persistedFinalState label step then surfaces the
NotFound signal to the caller after the database write, preserving
the kubeflow/pipelines#4484 stop-retrying contract.

Covered by a ReportWorkflowResource regression test asserting the run
reaches its terminal state and the caller still receives NotFound.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* fix(backend): align MLflow OnRunEnd test with permanent-failure semantics

TestReportWorkflow_WithMLflowOnRunEnd still asserted the pre-review
behavior where every plugin sync failure deferred the terminal report
with Unavailable. Since unavailable MLflow config is now classified as
a permanent plugin failure, the report succeeds: assert no error, keep
the PLUGIN_FAILED and config-unavailable output assertions, and also
assert the run reaches its terminal state.

message:
chore(deps): add Dependabot config for Go module version updates (#13491)

Adds `.github/dependabot.yml` enabling scheduled `gomod` version updates for
every Go module in the repo (`/`, `/api`, `/kubernetes_platform`,
`/third_party/ml-metadata`, `/test/tools/project-cleaner`).

The repo previously had no Dependabot config, so Go modules received no
scheduled version-update PRs and at least one security advisory
(golang.org/x/net, fixed in v0.55.0) went unactioned until it was bumped
manually in #13489. This makes Go dependency bumps explicit and deterministic.

- golang.org/x/* modules are grouped together (they release in lockstep).
- Remaining minor/patch bumps are batched to limit PR volume; major updates
  fall through to individual PRs for explicit review.
- npm/pip ecosystems are intentionally out of scope; Dependabot security
  updates are unaffected by this file.

Part of #13490.

The rebuild step's `if` condition lacked a status check function, so

after the first build fails, silently skipping the retry every time.

cancellation (important with fail-fast: true). Add `no-cache: true`
to bypass corrupt BuildKit cache layers that caused the original
failure. Fix the upload step with `always()` so it runs whether the

subject: ci: retry build dependency downloads (#13691)
message:
ci: retry build dependency downloads (#13691)

* ci: retry build dependency downloads

The protobuf tool chain fetches build dependencies with single-shot
network calls on the critical path of every workflow that uses the
protobuf composite action. A transient raw.githubusercontent.com error
failed both Kubernetes Native Migration lanes on #13690 at the same
second through the unretried wget in api/Makefile fetch-googleapis
(wget exit 8, run 28974863350).

Add bounded retries to the four single-shot fetches:
- api/Makefile fetch-googleapis: wget --tries=3 with backoff and
  retry on 429/5xx responses
- api/Makefile fetch-protobuf: retry the protobuf git clone up to
  three times, re-cloning into a clean directory each attempt
- backend/api/Makefile: same wget flags for the same status.proto
- protobuf composite action: curl --retry for the protoc release zip

Health-check curls in polling loops and the already-looped release
lookup in upgrade-test.yml are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* ci: fail protoc download on HTTP errors

Address review feedback: without --fail a persistent HTTP error (or a
404 from a bad protoc version input) exits zero and writes the error
page to the zip path, deferring the failure to a confusing unzip
error. With --fail, HTTP errors become curl errors, --retry-all-errors
retries them, and exhaustion fails the step at the download with a
clear message.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* ci: collect SeaweedFS diagnostics on E2E test failure

The intermittent E2E lane failures with 'dial tcp <seaweedfs>:9000:
i/o timeout' errors have three candidate causes that the existing
namespace log dump cannot distinguish: a crashed/restarted SeaweedFS
pod, node CPU/memory contention (the case a CPU request bump like this
one addresses), or a cluster dataplane failure on the ClusterIP path.

Add a targeted diagnostic script, invoked from the existing failure
log-collection step, that captures the SeaweedFS pod restart count and
last terminated state, its node's allocated-requests-vs-allocatable and
pressure conditions, and kube-proxy/endpoint state. Output goes to the
step log and the uploaded pod-log artifact. This turns the next
occurrence into evidence for whether the request bump is the right
lever, rather than an inference from failure shape. metrics-server is
not deployed in these clusters, so runtime CPU numbers are not
available; node allocated-requests stand in for scheduling contention.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* ci: harden SeaweedFS diagnostics arg parsing, pod selection, endpoints query

Address review feedback:
- Guard valued flags with ${2:?} so a missing value fails with a clear
  message instead of a set -u unbound-variable abort.
- Select the newest matching pod by creationTimestamp; a Recreate
  rollout can briefly leave a Terminating pod alongside the new one.
- Query Endpoints by service name. The SeaweedFS Service has no labels,
  so the label selector matched nothing while still exiting 0, which
  masked the miss and left the dataplane check silent.

subject: fix(backend): make MLflow experiment/run creation idempotently retryable (#13699)
message:
fix(backend): make MLflow experiment/run creation idempotently retryable (#13699)

* fix(backend): make MLflow experiment/run creation idempotently retryable

Under concurrent E2E load the single-worker MLflow server leaves a
create request queued past the per-call timeout, and the API server's
OnBeforeRunCreation create calls were the only MLflow calls excluded
from retry (noRetryPaths, to avoid duplicate server-side state). A
timed-out create therefore dropped the parent run silently, leaving
plugins_output without root_run_id/experiment_id and failing the
MLflow E2E tests intermittently.

Make the creates safe to retry instead of un-retried:
- CreateExperiment retries transient failures and, on RESOURCE_ALREADY_EXISTS
  (a concurrent or lost-response create), recovers the id via get-by-name.
- CreateRun retries transient failures when the tags carry the new
  IdempotencyTagKey (the stable KFP run id); before recreating it searches
  the experiment for a run already carrying that tag and reuses it, so a
  committed-but-lost-response create is never duplicated. Without the tag
  the run is created exactly once, unchanged.
- The dispatcher sizes the MLflow operation context to
  CreateMaxAttempts per-call timeouts so the retries fit within budget
  while the first attempt keeps the full per-call timeout (no regression).

The transport-level retryRoundTripper still does not blindly retry the
create paths; retry now happens at the method level where idempotency
is enforced. LogBatch is unchanged (MLflow params are immutable).

Covered by client tests for experiment already-exists recovery,
transient-retry-then-succeed, run idempotent recovery via search, and
single-shot create without the tag.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* fix(backend): address review on MLflow idempotent create

- CreateRun no longer recreates a run when the idempotency search cannot
  confirm the run's state. The search is retried on transient errors and
  returns a confirmed flag; an unconfirmed search fails the call rather
  than risking a duplicate run.
- Escape single quotes in the idempotency tag value before building the
  MLflow search filter, so a tag value can never alter the filter grammar.
- Size the MLflow operation context budget for every sequential create in
  the operation (experiment + run), so an earlier create's retries cannot
  consume the budget and cut a later create's retries short.

Adds a test asserting the run is not recreated when the search cannot
confirm its state.

subject: ci: give legacy v2 integration tests an intentional time budget (#13693)
message:
ci: give legacy v2 integration tests an intentional time budget (#13693)

* ci: give legacy v2 integration tests an honest time budget

The suite's normal runtime is about 9.5 minutes, dominated by cache
tests that execute sequential pipeline runs, while the go test binary
runs with Go's default 10-minute timeout: under a minute of headroom.
Ordinary lane slowness pushes the suite past the fuse and Go kills the
whole binary with 'panic: test timed out after 10m0s', discarding
every result. Ten of the lane failures in the last two days of PR CI
were this class; the panics list the interrupted test at 0s, showing
cumulative slowness rather than any hung test.

Set -timeout 20m (roughly 2x normal runtime, in line with the margins
past flake fixes settled on for this suite) and add
timeout-minutes: 40 to the job, which previously inherited GitHub's
6-hour default, so a genuinely hung suite now has a real ceiling.

Signed-off-by: ua74bf9844cc29a59 <ua74bf9844cc29a59@users.invalid>

* ci: annotate legacy v2 suite time budget overruns

When the go test -timeout fires, the only signal is a panic and
goroutine dump buried in the step log, which reads like a crash rather
than a budget breach. Tee the test output and, when the run fails with
'panic: test timed out after', emit a GitHub error annotation and a
job summary that state the budget, show the interrupted-test block,
explain that a near-zero elapsed time means cumulative slowness rather
than a hung test, and say what to do if it recurs. Non-timeout
failures are left untouched.

ci: authenticate googleapis proto fetches to avoid 429 rate limits (#13697)

* ci: authenticate googleapis proto fetches to avoid 429 rate limits

Follow-up to #13691, which added retries to these fetches. Retry treats
the symptom; the cause of the raw.githubusercontent.com failures is
anonymous per-IP rate limiting on shared CI egress IPs (same root cause
as the test-side 429s fixed in #13695). Send a bearer token from
GITHUB_TOKEN when set, passed through a temporary WGETRC file so the
token never appears on the command line or in an echoed recipe, and
plumb github.token into the protobuf composite action's proto-generation
step. If the authenticated fetch fails (e.g. token scoping) it falls
back to the anonymous fetch, so behavior is never worse than before;
both paths keep the retries.

WGETRC is used rather than --netrc-file (a curl-only flag) because it
makes wget send the Authorization header proactively; raw.githubusercontent
returns 429, not a 401 challenge, so netrc-style deferred auth would not
fire.
